topics.title: Safety: electrical supply, steam and faults
topics.text:
Safety precautions
Always follow these instructions
These instructions must be followed to prevent personal injury and damage to property.
■ The severity of harm or damage from incorrect use is classiﬁed as follows.
WARNING Risk of death or serious injury.
CAUTION
Risk of minor injury or damage to
property.
■ The following symbols indicate the instructions to follow.
Prohibited actions.
Required actions.
WARNING
To prevent ﬁre, burns and
electric shock...
Do not touch the steam vent.
• Take particular care
around children.
(Risk of burns.)
• Do not damage the power cord or plug.
Do not scratch, modify, place near hot
surfaces, bend forcefully, twist, pull, place
heavy objects on, bundle or pinch them.
(Risk of electric shock or ﬁre from a short circuit.)
→ Consult your retailer for repairs.
• Do not use a damaged cord or a
loose outlet.
(Risk of electric shock or ﬁre from a
short circuit.)
• Do not connect or disconnect the plug
with wet hands. (Risk of electric shock.)
• Use a dedicated 100 V AC outlet
rated at 15 A or higher.
(Risk of electric shock or ﬁre.)
• Insert the plug fully.
(Risk of smoke, ﬁre or electric shock.)
• Remove dust from the plug regularly.
(Dust on the pins can absorb moisture,
compromise insulation and cause a ﬁre.)
→ Unplug and wipe with a dry cloth.
Power plug and cord
If an abnormality or fault occurs,
stop using the appliance
immediately and unplug it.
(Risk of smoke, ﬁre, electric shock or injury.)
Examples of abnormalities or faults
• The plug or cord becomes unusually hot.
• The cord is damaged or power is
intermittent.
• The appliance becomes deformed or
unusually hot.
• An unusual rotating noise occurs during
operation.
→ Ask your retailer to inspect and repair it
immediately.

topics.title: Safe placement, hot parts and handling
topics.text:
CAUTION
To prevent ﬁre and
burns...
• Keep out of reach of
young children.
• Do not let children or
people unfamiliar with
the appliance use it
unsupervised.
(Risk of burns, electric
shock or injury.)
• Do not immerse the
appliance in water or
splash it with water.
(Risk of electric shock or
ﬁre from a short circuit.)
• Never disassemble,
repair or modify the
appliance yourself.
(Risk of ﬁre, electric
shock or injury.)
→ Consult your retailer
for repairs.
To prevent accidents...
• Do not use on an unstable surface or a tablecloth.
• Take care where you set down the hot bread pan. (Risk of falling or
ﬁre.)
• Do not use on carpets or other heat-sensitive coverings. (Risk of ﬁre.)
• Do not use on surfaces made slippery by ﬂour, grease or dust.
• Remove ﬂour and other deposits and place at least 10 cm from
the edge.
(The appliance may slip and fall.)
• Do not use close to walls or furniture.
• Leave at least 5 cm clearance.
(Risk of deformation or
discolouration.)
• Do not touch hot parts such as
the bread pan, appliance body,
vents, interior, heater or inner lid.
(Risk of burns.)
→ Always use oven mitts to
remove the bread pan.
• Do not use wet mitts.
(They conduct heat readily and
may cause burns.)
Handling the appliance and bread pan
Power plug
• Do not touch hot parts during use or
for a while afterwards. (Risk of burns.)
• Measure ingredients and select programs correctly.
(Dough that scatters or overﬂows can burn on the heater,
producing smoke or causing a malfunction.)
• Unplug when not in use.
(Risk of electric shock or ﬁre from electrical leakage.)
• Always hold the plug, not the cord, when unplugging.
(Risk of electric shock or ﬁre from a short circuit.)
• Do not press on the base of the cord when storing the plug in
the cord compartment (p. 6).
(Risk of electric shock or ﬁre from a short circuit.)
• Do not cover the lid with a cloth or similar
item.
• Keep the handle lowered during use.
• Do not place in a damp area or near a ﬂame.
• Do not apply excessive force to the
parts shown on the right.
(Risk of damage or deformation.)
• If you have food allergies, consult your doctor before use.
• This appliance is not designed for use in vehicles, boats or outdoors.

topics.title: Manual mode: levels and limits
topics.text:
About manual mode
Use individual stages of the bread-making process. Select Knead, Rise or Bake, then set the
level and time.
• When using Knead or Rise, check the dough’s condition as appropriate for the bread you are
making.
Knead
Bake
Rise
Rotation speed levels for diﬀerent tasks
• Level 1: combining ﬂour or making marbled
dough
• Level 2: low speed / mixing in extra ingredients
• Level 3: medium speed
• Level 4: high speed
• For 30 seconds after starting, or restarting after a pause, the blade turns slowly to
prevent ﬂour from scattering. It then changes to the selected speed.
• The level can be changed after starting. During the ﬁrst 30 seconds of slow
rotation, however, the change takes eﬀect only when that period has ended.
Time settings: Levels 1, 2 and 3: 1–30 minutes
Level 4: 1–15 minutes
Baking temperature levels for diﬀerent breads
• Level 1: brioche / white breads (light crust)
• Level 2: pain de mie / white breads (medium crust)
• Level 3: rye / wholemeal / white breads (dark crust)
• Level 4: French bread
• The level can be changed after starting.
Time settings: 30–50 minutes
• If the bread is not baked enough when the program ﬁnishes, you
can use Additional Baking.
Additional baking: up to 2 times*
* Available until the total set baking time reaches 50
minutes. After 50 minutes, “U50” appears on the display
and additional baking is unavailable. (p.101)
Rising temperature levels for diﬀerent uses
• Level 1: resting / bench rest
• Level 2: crusty breads
• Level 3: white breads and enriched breads
• Level 4: prooﬁng after shaping / ﬁnal prooﬁng
• The level can be changed after starting.
Time settings: 10–120 minutes
• Capacity: 200–300 g ﬂour
• For ingredients that must not be used during Knead, see “Take care with these ingredients!” on p.22.
• Always pause the machine before checking the dough during operation.

dried natural
yeast are not
dispensed
automatically.

topics.text:
Cleaning
To avoid damaging
parts…
Bread pan / blades
Lid
Remove any remaining
dough and rinse with water.
1 Pour warm water into the bread pan and leave
it to soak for a while.
• If the blade is
diﬃcult to remove,
turn it left and right,
then pull it oﬀ.
2 Thoroughly wash the bread pan and
blade with water and a sponge.
• If there is a white ﬁlm
on the blade, wash it
with mild dishwashing
detergent. Residue
makes dough more
likely to stick and can
leave the blade inside
the loaf.
• Do not leave dough around the mounting shaft.
This can damage the pan’s ﬂuororesin coating.
3 Use a bamboo skewer to
remove dough caught in the
blade or mounting shaft.
• Dough left on the mounting shaft
can make the blade come oﬀ more
easily or remain inside the loaf.
Wipe with a well-
wrung damp cloth.
• After wiping the dispensing
valve with a damp cloth, check
that the ingredient opening is
closed.
Starter
container
Wash thoroughly with mild
dishwashing detergent and dry.
• Starter residue allows bacteria to multiply
and cause spoilage, preventing the next
starter batch from developing properly.
■ If spoilage occurs:
1 Soak in diluted chlorine-based kitchen
bleach.
2 Rinse thoroughly.

topics.title: Ingredients: flour, substitutions, half loaves and starter storage
topics.text:
Frequently asked
questions
Ingredients
Can I use any brand of
Japanese wheat ﬂour?
Use Japanese bread ﬂour with a high protein content (at least 11%). Many ﬂours made
from Japanese wheat are lower in protein. Protein content varies by brand and harvest
season, so results and loaf height will vary.
Can I use Japanese
wheat ﬂour in recipes
other than those on the
recipe book’s back cover?
You can try, but the loaf will be smaller and chewier. (Try reducing the water in
the basic recipe by 10 g (mL).)
It is not recommended for Soft White Bread, French Bread and similar
programs because their characteristic texture will be lost.
Can I use
specialist ﬂour?
White bread
Yes, but adjust the water. The loaf may rise too much or develop a cavity near
the top, so reduce the water by 5–10%.
French bread
Yes, but the result and loaf height vary depending on the specialist ﬂour used.
Udon (medium-strength
ﬂour)
If the dough is too ﬁrm, add 10 g (mL) more water. If it is too soft, reduce the
water by 10 g (mL).
Can I substitute
another ingredient for
butter or shortening?
Yes. Solid fats such as butter, margarine and shortening can be substituted in
equal amounts.
• Diﬀerent fats may make the crust lighter or darker, or aﬀect the result.
Can I substitute
another ingredient
for skim milk
powder?
Yes.
6 g skim milk powder (1 large spoon) is equivalent to 70 g milk (about 70
mL).
• When using milk, reduce the water by the same amount.
Can I use quantities from
a commercially published
cookbook?
The quantities in this manual are tailored to this bread maker. Diﬀerent quantities may not
give good results.
Can I make a
half loaf?
Only the Half Loaf program (p.40) can be used. Halving the ingredients in other
programs does not suit the machine’s process: kneading and resting (degassing),
for example, may be too vigorous.
Can I use homemade
natural yeast?
Its fermentation strength tends to be inconsistent, so it will not give reliable
results.
We recommend Hoshino Natural Yeast Bread Starter,
which has relatively consistent fermentation strength.
How should I store
natural yeast granules
and prepared starter?
Natural yeast granules (p.15)
Sensitive to high temperatures: seal tightly and refrigerate.
• Use before the best-before date (valid for unopened
products stored as directed).
Prepared starter
(p.45)
Keep in the starter container with the lid on and refrigerate.
• Use within one week.
Scan the QR code for
detailed support
information.
Do not freeze or store at
room temperature.
(Fermentation strength
will be lost.)

topics.title: Ingredients: yeast, rice flour, rice and freezing dough
topics.text:
Ingredients
How should I store
dry yeast and dried
natural yeast?
Refrigerate. (After opening, seal tightly and use promptly.)
• Use before the best-before date (valid for unopened products stored as
directed).
• Do not freeze. (Condensation may prevent the yeast from dropping out of the
dispenser.)
Can bread mixes be
used with natural
yeast programs?
Dried Natural Yeast Bread program
White bread mix and soft white bread mix can be used.
Instead of the supplied dry yeast, put 5 g dried natural yeast
per bag of bread mix into the yeast dispenser.
Natural Yeast Bread program
White bread mix and sweet white bread mix can be used.
Instead of the supplied dry yeast, use 25 g prepared starter (2
large spoons) and 170 g (mL) water per bag of bread mix.
Can I make rice ﬂour
bread with ordinary
rice ﬂour (joshinko)?
Do I have to use
the speciﬁed ﬂour?
Joshinko contains no gluten and its particles are coarse, so bread cannot be
made from it alone.
Always use the speciﬁed ﬂour for the Rice Flour Bread (with wheat / no wheat)
programs.
Ordinary rice ﬂour (joshinko) can replace up to 20% of the total ﬂour in a wheat-
ﬂour bread. (Bake using program 3, White Bread.)
Can I use a diﬀerent
bread-making rice ﬂour
for Rice Flour Bread
(with wheat)?
No. Rice ﬂours produce doughs of diﬀerent ﬁrmness even with the same
recipe, so the dough cannot be kneaded properly.
What cooked rice can I
use for Cooked-rice
Bread / Rice French
Bread?
Use cooled cooked white rice, preferably at 30°C or below. Refrigerated rice
can also be used. If it has clumped together, loosen it ﬁrst with the recipe’s
water to help it mix (p.94).
Thaw frozen rice and allow it to reach room temperature before use.
Use rice that has been kept warm for no more than 12 hours, and cool it
before use.
Can I freeze the cookie
dough for melon bread
before use?
Yes. Thaw it naturally beforehand and make sure it is not too ﬁrm when placing
it on the bread dough.
Where can I buy durum
semolina ﬂour?
It is available at department stores throughout Japan.
What ﬂour should I use for
dusting?
We recommend bread ﬂour when shaping bread, and potato starch for mochi.
(Cornstarch, bread ﬂour and similar ﬂours can also be used.)
Can I use glutinous
rice soaked
overnight?
Yes, but it becomes too soft, so this is generally not recommended. Reduce the
water to allow for what the rice has absorbed: 80 g (mL) for 2 go, or 140 g (mL)
for 3 go.
When needed | Frequently asked questions

Bread

topics.title: After baking: slicing, removing, freezing and storing bread
topics.text:
Frequently asked
questions
After baking / completion
Why is my loaf small
when I use Japanese
wheat ﬂour?
Some brands of Japanese wheat ﬂour have a lower protein content
and may produce a smaller loaf.
Can I bake a square-
topped loaf?
This bread maker produces domed loaves: the dough expands upwards during baking
(oven spring).
How can I slice
bread neatly?
Bread is diﬃcult to slice straight after baking. Wait a little
before slicing.
• Lay the loaf on its side and move a bread knife back and forth.
Why is the
bread diﬃcult to
remove?
If it is still diﬃcult to remove after taking out the bread pan and letting it cool for about
2 minutes, return the pan to the machine for 5–10 minutes, then try again. (p.32)
• Leaving it too long may cause the loaf to shrink and its sides to collapse.
• Do not use a knife, fork, chopsticks or similar utensil to remove the
bread. (This damages the ﬂuororesin coating.)
Why is dough left on the
kneading blade?
Low-viscosity (soft) dough may stick to the blade. Remove the remaining dough and rinse
the blade with water. (p.86)
What can I do with bread
trimmings?
Use them to make rusks or breadcrumbs.
Can I freeze
bread or dough?
White bread
Slice, wrap each slice individually in plastic wrap and freeze. For
the best ﬂavour, freeze bread while it is as fresh as possible.
• For best ﬂavour, keep frozen for about one month.
Butter rolls
After shaping and prooﬁng, arrange on a tray, cover with plastic wrap and
freeze. Once frozen, transfer to a plastic bag.
To bake, thaw at 30–35°C, brush with beaten egg and bake.
• If short of time, brush with beaten egg while still frozen and add about 5 minutes to the baking time.
Pizza
Wrap the rolled-out dough in plastic wrap and freeze.
To bake, add toppings to the frozen dough and bake.
Why does bread
made with natural
yeast diﬀer slightly
from bread made with
dry yeast?
Texture and ﬂavour vary with the natural yeast used. Natural yeast bread
generally has these characteristics:
• A slightly smaller loaf and darker crust
• A distinctive ﬂavour: the crust smells somewhat like rice crackers or soy sauce, with a mildly sour and sweet taste
• A slightly coarser crumb
• A chewy, substantial texture
During baking, it also gives oﬀ a fermented smell similar to yoghurt.
Why is dry yeast still
visible in dough made
with a dough program?
As long as it has been kneaded into the dough, this is not a problem. It will
work during dividing, shaping and the second rise.
90

topics.title: After baking: blades, dough and dispenser leftovers
topics.text:
After baking / completion
Why is the dough soft?
Try reducing the water by 5–10 g (mL). Dusting with ﬂour makes the dough easier to
handle.
Why does the kneading
blade remain in the loaf?
As the bread rises, the blade may unlock and come out with the loaf.
Always remove it before slicing, as cutting the loaf with the blade inside
will damage the blade.
Why can’t I remove
the kneading blade?
Dough has hardened around the mounting shaft.
Pour warm water into the pan and leave to soak. Then turn the blade left
and right and pull it oﬀ. (p.86)
Why does the blade come
oﬀ during operation?
Dough hardened on the mounting shaft prevents the blade from ﬁtting securely. Clean the
blade and mounting shaft. (p.86)
Why hasn’t the dough
risen much in the
bread dough or pizza
dough program?
Some recipes ferment more slowly. After the bread dough or pizza dough
program ends, leave the lid closed to allow more rising time. (Approx. 20–30
minutes.)
Can I reuse dough
from an
unsuccessful batch?
For example, dough
that has not been
baked…
You can use it for doughnuts, pizza and similar recipes. Check the
stage at which the machine stopped, then proceed as follows.
Programs using dry yeast or dried natural yeast
• If yeast remains in the yeast dispenser:
Use program d3 (Enriched Dough) to make dough for doughnuts
(Recipe Book p.33), or d5 (Pizza Dough) to make pizza dough (Recipe
Book p.36).
• If no yeast remains in the yeast dispenser:
Remove the dough and make doughnuts (Recipe Book
p.33) or pizza (Recipe Book p.36).
Programs using natural yeast
Remove the dough and make doughnuts (Recipe Book p.33).
Why does the pasta feel
diﬀerent from commercially
sold dried pasta?
The preparation method diﬀers from dried pasta, so its appearance, ﬁrmness and
elasticity are diﬀerent.
Why are the noodles
diﬃcult to cut?
Measure accurately and dust the dough thoroughly with ﬂour.
The ﬂuororesin
coating on the bread
pan or another part
has peeled.
Can I still use it?
Hard ingredients may cause the ﬂuororesin coating on the pan or other parts
to peel. (p.22)
Accidentally swallowing a ﬂake of this coating does not cause harm to the
body.
Ingredients remain in the
raisin/nut dispenser.
Depending on the ingredient and how it is processed, some may remain in the dispenser.
You can set the buzzer (♪) and add them by hand.
When needed | Frequently asked questions

topics.title: Bread appearance: collapse, holes, flour, crust and melted chocolate
topics.text:
Problem
What to check
Bread: shape
Does not rise at all
(white and lumpy
throughout)
Dry yeast /
dried natural
yeast /
prepared starter
• Did you forget to add it?
• Was it stored poorly, or has its best-before date or use-by
period passed?
• Did you use baking powder by mistake?
• Did you forget to ﬁt the kneading blade?
• Was there a power failure during operation?
Shape and rise
vary from day to
day
• Homemade bread varies in shape and rise from day to day under conditions such as these:
Room temperature: High temperatures (such as in summer), or changes during operation
(for example, switching oﬀ the air conditioner).
Ingredient type / quality: Flour with less protein than usual; dry yeast or similar ingredients
stored poorly or past their best-before date.
Sticky bottom
or deeply
sunken sides
• Did you remove the loaf from the pan immediately after baking and let it
cool on a raised wire rack?
• In a warm room, reducing the water by 10 g (mL) may help.
Sunken top
(crust is baked)
Flat, square
top
Collapses
• Did you use too little ﬂour?
• Did you use too much water?
For Wholemeal Bread:
• This is more likely with a high proportion of wholemeal ﬂour or certain types of ﬂour.
For Rice Flour Bread (no wheat):
• A white, ﬂat top is normal.
• Did you add ingredients not listed in the recipe, such as dairy products or cocoa?
• Did you use the wrong type of oil?
• Did you add the fat listed in the recipe?
Large hole
in the
bottom /
crushed loaf
• The kneading blade will leave an impression.
• Did you touch the underside of the bread pan while
removing the loaf? (This may turn the blade and
damage the bread.)
Flour remains around the
outside
• Did you use too much ﬂour?
• Did you use too little water?
Bread: other issues
The crust is not the
colour I expected.
Parts of the top
burn.
• Change the crust setting (p.23) or adjust the sugar. Less sugar gives a
slightly lighter crust; more gives a slightly darker crust.
• If the loaf rises above the pan, reduce the dry yeast, dried natural yeast or
water.
• Oven spring may make the top look as though it has peeled away.
Hard crust
• Let the loaf cool until just warm, then put it in a plastic bag to soften the crust slightly.
Chocolate melts even
with Gentle Mixing.
• The dough’s rising temperature is above chocolate’s melting point, so it
may melt. Keep the chocolate frozen until just before adding it. Large pieces
can obstruct the blade: use chocolate chips or chop into cubes no larger than
5 mm.
Do not turn.
When needed | Troubleshooting results

topics.title: Results: sticky dough, croissants, rice grains and melon bread
topics.text:
Problem
What to check
Bread: other issues
Extra ingredients collect on
one side.
• Distribution can vary with the ingredient type, dough ﬁrmness and other factors.
Shaped and proofed
dough is slack and
sticky.
• Over-proofed dough sags and becomes slack. Rising time varies by bread,
but generally, if you lightly press the side of the risen dough with a ﬁngertip
and it slowly springs back, prooﬁng is complete.
Croissants do
not turn out well.
• If the butter enclosed in the dough melts, proper layers
will not form. Chill the dough thoroughly before enclosing
the butter.
• In a warm room, butter melts more easily, so chill for
longer.
60-
minute
bread
Does not rise
• Did you use lukewarm water (35–40°C)?
• Did you dissolve the dry yeast at the start of preparation?
Cooked-rice bread / Rice French bread
Rice grains remain.
• Put the rice and the recipe’s water in a separate container, loosen the rice thoroughly,
then add it to the bread pan.
Low-carb bread
Sunken sides
• Did you use a medium egg?
• Too high a proportion of egg may make the loaf rise too much and its sides sink.
• Did you use cold water when the room was 25°C or below?
• If the sunken sides bother you, reduce the water by 10 g (mL).
Troubleshooting results
Custom bread
Melon bread
The cookie
topping cracks.
• Did you mix the cookie dough thoroughly?
• Did you bring the cookie dough together until smooth?
• Did you try to wrap the cookie dough tightly around the bread dough?
• Simply place it on top. (Press lightly to make it adhere for a neat
shape.)
• Did you score the grid pattern too deeply?
The cookie
dough becomes
soft and slack.
• The butter melted while softening, leaving too much liquid in the
dough.
• Once the butter has melted, the dough will tend to sag and tear even
after chilling.
The cookie topping is
uneven.
• Did you reposition the bread dough in the centre?

topics.text:
Problem
What to check
Custom bread
Melon bread
The cookie
topping does
not stay on top.
• Is the cookie dough too cold and ﬁrm?
• When “Work in 10 minutes” appears, take the cookie dough out of the
refrigerator and roll it out. It should be ﬂexible enough to bend easily.
The cookie
topping
protrudes from
the pan.
• Did you lightly press the edges when placing the cookie dough on top?
• Pushing it in will make the surface crack during baking.
Sweet bean
buns
A cavity
forms inside.
• Bread dough rises, but sweet bean paste does not expand in the same way.
Steam from the ﬁlling pushes the dough upwards, creating a cavity. This is
not a problem.
Brioche
Oil collects at the
bottom / butter is
unevenly distributed.
• Was the butter for adding later cut into 1 cm cubes?

the later addition?

Much ﬂour remains
when making rice ﬂour
bread without wheat.

with wheat does
not turn out well.

(High room temperatures can impair the result.)

Hard crust
The crust is not
completely
white.

• The crust will brown slightly.

Not enough rise
• Did you add baking powder?
(Dry yeast or dried natural yeast will not make it rise.)
• Did you use the speciﬁed quantities?
Uneven butter distribution
(uneven colour, cavities,
etc.)
• Did you cut the butter into 1 cm cubes?

around the
outside.

Below
5 cm

The result is sticky.

Chocolate ganache
The mixture separates.
• Cream with a high milk-fat content (41% or above) combined with high-
cocoa chocolate may separate. Adding 10 g milk (about 10 mL) makes
separation less likely.
Too soft
• Chocolate with a high milk content gives a softer result. Reduce the cream by 10–20

the sides of the
bread pan.

topics.title: Results: milk jam, jam, fruit compote and amazake
topics.text:
Problem
What to check
Milk jam
The mixture separates.
• Is the cream old?
Too soft
• Did you use the speciﬁed quantities?
Too ﬁrm
• Did you use the speciﬁed quantities?
• Leaving it in the bread pan instead of removing it promptly may make
it ﬁrm, as residual heat continues to cook it.
Lumps form.
• When pouring the ﬁnished milk jam into a container, including the solids stuck to the
pan’s sides can cause lumps.
It sticks to the sides
of the pan.
• This happens as the mixture reduces. Scrape out just the mixture
around the sides and allow it to set: it becomes like soft caramel and can
be eaten as it is.
Jam
Does not set
(not thick)
The jam is relatively runny because it is lower in sugar and contains no additives.
• Underripe, overripe or stale fruit may have too little pectin to set well.
• Did you use too much fruit?
• Did you reduce the sugar or lemon juice?
(Jam needs the right amounts of sugar, acid and pectin to set.)
Fruit compote
The fruit falls apart.
• Was it overripe?
• Some fruit varieties break down more readily.
Some parts have not
absorbed enough
syrup.
• Did you cover the fruit with a paper-towel drop lid?
• After removing it from the syrup, place the less-soaked portions face down
in the syrup and leave to cool.
• It is best eaten after resting for half a day to one day.
Amazake
Lumps form.
• Is the kneading blade ﬁtted?
• Did you break up the cooked rice and koji when adding them?
Rice grains stick
to the sides.
• Did you scrape down the rice grains?
• Did you break up the cooked rice and koji when adding them?
It does not become
sweet.
• Is the koji old?
• Was the koji stored correctly? If it is past its best-before date or was
stored poorly, the amazake may not become sweet.
• Did you use the speciﬁed quantities?
• Did you add the ingredients in the correct order? Mixing hot rice directly
with koji may prevent sweetness from developing.
• Did you use hot water? This raises the overall temperature and may
prevent sweetness from developing.
• Did you use sake lees? This program makes rice-koji amazake; sake lees
cannot be used.

topics.title: Machine troubleshooting: buttons, dispensers, stopping, timer and sounds
topics.text:
Is it a fault?
These are not faults. Check the following before requesting service.
Problem
Cause
Remedy
Buttons do not respond.
• Is the power plug unplugged?
Insert the power plug.
It does not run (knead)
after Start.
• Rice Flour Bread (with wheat) starts with a resting stage, so it does not move at ﬁrst.
Dry yeast or dried
natural yeast
does not drop.
• Automatic dispensing time varies with the program and room temperature.
• The yeast dispenser is wet or has a
static charge.
Wipe with a well-wrung damp
cloth and allow to air-dry.
• Is the dry yeast or dried natural yeast
damp or covered in condensation?
Use fresh dry yeast or dried natural
yeast.
Extra ingredients
do not drop from
the raisin/nut
dispenser.
• Are the ingredients heaped up?
Spread them level.
Operation stopped
partway through.
(The current time is
displayed.)
• Manual mode was left paused for 15 minutes.

longer than about 10 minutes during
preparation.
If it stopped while still at the dough
stage, the dough can be reused.
(p.91)
I cannot set the
desired timer time.
• Are you trying to set a time outside
the allowed range? The time required
to ﬁnish baking varies by program.
[Example of timer range]
Program: Pain de mie
Current time: 8:30 p.m.
(Display: “20:30”)
Available ﬁnish times: 1:20 a.m.–
9:30 a.m.
(“1:20”–“9:30”)

• Sandwich bread: 3–13 h
• Cooked-rice bread: 4–13 h

min–13 h

It starts kneading
immediately even
though I set the timer.

Bread, French Bread, Rye Bread, Wholemeal Bread, Pale-crust Bread, Half Loaf,

stage starts immediately when the timer is started. (pp.8–9)
There are noises
during operation
or while waiting
on the timer.
The following sounds are normal:
• When kneading or degassing dough, or pounding mochi:
“Creaking / slapping”: dough being kneaded
“Whirring”: the motor turning
“Clattering”: mochi being pounded

“Clunking”: the dispensing valve or ﬂap opening

topics.text:
If these messages appear…
Problem
Cause
Remedy
Rotation stops
partway through.
(The blade does
not turn.)
• Too many ingredients, or hard ingredients caught in the blade, overload the motor and
activate its protective device, stopping rotation. (The ingredients remain as ﬂour and are not
baked even when the program ﬁnishes.)

topics.title: U50 — oven chamber is hot
topics.text:
Cause: The oven chamber is hot (40°C or above), for example after baking. In manual Bake mode, additional baking has been used twice or the total time has exceeded 50 minutes.
Remedy: Open the lid and allow the oven chamber to cool thoroughly. About 1 hour immediately after completion.

topics.title: U53 — motor overloaded
topics.text:
Cause: The motor is overloaded.
Remedy: Measure the ingredients accurately. Crush large pieces, such as walnuts, before adding them. Press Cancel.

topics.title: H01–H99 — fault
topics.text:
Cause: A fault has occurred.
Remedy: Contact your retailer for repairs.

topics.title: Power outage display
topics.text: Indicates a power failure during preparation. After an outage of up to 10 minutes, operation resumes automatically when power returns. The bread’s quality may be affected. This also appears after preparation if the machine was unplugged and plugged back in during operation.

topics.title: Yeast does not drop
topics.text:
Automatic dispensing time varies with the program and room temperature.
Cause: The yeast dispenser is wet or has a static charge. Remedy: Wipe with a well-wrung damp cloth and allow to air-dry.
Cause: The dry yeast or dried natural yeast is damp or covered in condensation. Remedy: Use fresh dry yeast or dried natural yeast.

topics.title: Clean the bread pan and blades
topics.text:
Remove any remaining dough and rinse with water.
1. Pour warm water into the bread pan and leave it to soak for a while. If the blade is difficult to remove, turn it left and right, then pull it off.
2. Thoroughly wash the bread pan and blade with water and a sponge. If there is a white film on the blade, wash it with mild dishwashing detergent. Residue makes dough more likely to stick and can leave the blade inside the loaf. Do not leave dough around the mounting shaft: this can damage the pan’s fluororesin coating.
3. Use a bamboo skewer to remove dough caught in the blade or mounting shaft. Dough left on the mounting shaft can make the blade come off more easily or remain inside the loaf.
Wash and dry promptly. Do not wash in a dishwasher. Avoid alkaline or mildly alkaline cleaners, chlorine-based cleaner, scouring powder, metal scourers, the nylon side of a sponge and mesh-covered sponges. The separate starter-container spoilage procedure permits diluted chlorine-based kitchen bleach; it is not a bread-pan cleaning instruction.

topics.title: Clean the yeast and raisin/nut dispensers
topics.text:
Yeast dispenser: Wipe with a well-wrung damp cloth and allow to air-dry. Do not dry-wipe: static electricity may prevent the yeast from dropping.
Raisin/nut dispenser: Pull upwards to remove, press to open the flap, and wash with mild dishwashing detergent. Remove all oily residue.
Upper lid: Open to 70–90° and pull upwards to remove; wipe with a well-wrung damp cloth.
Main unit: Wipe with a well-wrung damp cloth. Remove flour, ingredients and extra ingredients scattered inside the oven chamber. Oil residue or water droplets may collect around the steam vent.
